The Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tenses vs. Regular Future Tenses

You use the Future Continuous tense to talk about something that will be in progress at a certain point in the future.
Future Continuous is also used to talk about what we assume is happening at a certain period of time.

For example:
Don't call my dad. He will be reading.

You use the Future Perfect tense to talk about an action in the future that occurred before another action in the future.
Future Continuous is also used to talk about what we assume is happening at a certain period of time.
The Future Perfect tense describes what will have happened in the future before a different action takes place, or by a specific time.

For example:
By Friday this week, I will have customized my résumés and I will have built my own online portfolio.
In the near future, résumés will have become obsolete.

images.text: It has been a while now since I was laid-off at Polygon. I have had a few interviews, but so far, no takers, but I think next week I will be exploring a few new leads. The seminar on job skills building this weekend was very useful. In the workshop, our teacher bestowed on us some valuable insights and tips. For example, he told us to make our cover letters brief. He also gave us advice on building the résumé. He told us to change our résumé outline based on the job we were searching for. He said it was important to our job search to tailor our résumé to the company's particular needs.

He also explained how important it was that a good résumé is standard, and nothing special.
“Many of you are going to be missing out on great job opportunities because your résumé is too flamboyant,” he said.
He explained that a good or great résumé doesn't make the person. You and your interview make the person.

Finally, our teacher inquired as to who had an online presence? Silence.
He asked us who had a profile online that prospective bosses could explore at a click of a button?
He went onto explain that in the near future, résumés will have become obsolete. Everything will be done through social media and that nothing is going to be paper based.
“Build your brand online,” he said. “You will be needing it in the years ahead.”
I will be taking his advice to heart and by Friday this week, I will have customized my résumés and I will have built my own online portfolio.

I feel energized now.
